symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed integer that does not vary with \(n\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of labeled experimental units.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_K
symbols.def: The class of contrasts satisfying the three member properties in \(\mathrm{def:contrast\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: A generic index for a contrast-orthogonal basis vector.

symbols.name: d_j
symbols.def: A basis vector chosen so that \(d_1,\ldots,d_{J-1}\) span \(\ker(c^\top)\).

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: A generic vector of active-arm binary potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: A generic argument of the response-alphabet gauge.

symbols.name: \phi
symbols.def: A real function with weak derivative \(\phi'\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_n
symbols.def: A probability law for \(Z\) selected without observing \(y\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_n^\star
symbols.def: The product assignment law with one-unit probabilities \(q^\star\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau
symbols.def: Any Markov kernel from the full labeled observed data to a reported contrast, with deterministic estimators included.

symbols.name: R_n(c)
symbols.def: The design-estimator game value defined in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\).

symbols.name: \ell^\star
symbols.def: The lexicographically least dual optimizer in \(\mathrm{def:dual\text{-}score}\).

symbols.name: \phi_{\kappa}
symbols.def: The positive even unit-norm minimizer of \(\int_{\mathbb R}\{4|f'|^2+\kappa(c)|x|f^2\}\,dx\).

symbols.name: H(q)
symbols.def: \(H(q)=\sum_{a\in S_c}c_a^2/q_a\), with value \(\infty\) when an active \(q_a\) is zero.

symbols.name: \Pi_n
symbols.def: A prior generated by the full-dimensional response-tube handle in \(\mathrm{def:tube\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{BR}_{\Pi_n}(r)
symbols.def: The posterior squared-error risk for \(\tau_c(y)\) under \(\Pi_n\), conditional on any fixed assignment vector with count vector \(r\).

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: The all-future sample-size threshold returned by the certificate.

symbols.name: \mathbb A_{\mathrm R}
symbols.def: The field of real algebraic numbers represented by a square-free polynomial in \(\mathbb Z[x]\), a rational isolating interval, and Thom-sign data; field operations and order comparisons use exact rational arithmetic, resultants, and Sturm sequences.

symbols.name: B_n
symbols.def: The exact rational or real-algebraic lower risk witness computed for the requested sample size \(n\).

symbols.name: U_n
symbols.def: The exact rational or real-algebraic upper risk witness computed for the requested sample size \(n\).

symbols.name: \Gamma
symbols.def: A finite encoded record containing \(N\), rational and real-algebraic gauge data, finite spline and response-tube schemas, finite estimator schemas, symbolic monotone remainder inequalities, and proof-checkable evaluator code.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Eval}_{\Gamma}
symbols.def: The total generator encoded by \(\Gamma\) that maps each requested integer \(n\ge N\) to the exact pair \((B_n,U_n)\).

symbols.name: \mathsf{Cert}
symbols.def: A proof-producing procedure that returns the finite record \(\Gamma\) specified in \(\mathrm{def:effective\text{-}certificate}\).

standard.name: Scale normalization for a treatment contrast

novel.justification: This proposal-specific restriction isolates the genuinely multi-arm response geometry: with at least three active coordinates, \(\ker(c^\top)\subset\mathbb R^{S_c}\) has dimension at least two, so the response tube has multiple transverse directions absent from the normalized two-arm experiment. Prespecified regimen-versus-average contrasts in four-arm trials, including an ACTG-175-style comparison, satisfy the restriction.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal D_n\) is selected independently of the fixed schedule \(y\).

definitions.name: Response-alphabet dual score
definitions.construction: Choose the lexicographically least \(\ell^\star\) solving \[\max_{\ell\in\mathbb R^{S_c}}\ell^\top v\quad\text{subject to}\quad |\ell^\top b_t|\le\theta_t^2\ \text{for all }t\in\mathcal T_c,\] and set \(g^\star=\ell^\star/\kappa(c)\).

definitions.name: Contrast-weighted independent allocation
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal D_n^\star\) draw \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) independently with \(\Pr(Z_i=a)=q_a^\star\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A_K\).

definitions.name: Total full-label nonlinear Airy rule
definitions.construction: On observations produced by \(\mathrm{def:independent\text{-}qstar\text{-}design}\), set \[\delta_n^\star=\operatorname{proj}_{[-1,1]}\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nT_i-n^{-2/3}h_{\kappa}\left(n^{-2/3}\sum_{i=1}^nU_i\right)\right\}.\] Define the rule to equal zero on every label-outcome string outside the support of that design.

definitions.name: Full-dimensional exact-target response-tube handle
definitions.construction: Start with the invertible basis \(B=[v,d_1,\ldots,d_{J-1}]\), where \(d_j\) span \(\ker(c^\top)\). Represent each of \(\pm v\) and \(\pm d_j\) by nonnegative weights on \(\mathcal T_c\); localize the target coordinate with squared compact rational splines approximating \(\phi_{\kappa}^2\), localize every transverse coordinate with endpoint-vanishing rational polynomial densities, and form a permutation-invariant finite-schedule prior. The sought construction must retain exact target regression, join sign cells by weak integration by parts, and stratify counts into local, positive exterior, inactive-arm, and missing-active-arm faces.

definitions.name: Finite exact all-future risk certificate
definitions.construction: For rational \(c\in\mathcal C_K\) and rational \(\eta>0\), enumerate finite rational primal-dual gauge records, compact rational spline records, ordered-real-algebraic response-tube records, and rationalized total Airy-rule records. Use the representation of \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm R}\) by square-free integer polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and Thom-sign data, with exact rational field operations, resultants, Sturm sequences, and certified order comparisons. Return the first finite record \(\Gamma\) containing \(N\), the finite symbolic data, proof-checkable monotone remainder bounds, and code for a total evaluator \(\mathsf{Eval}_{\Gamma}\). On each requested integer \(n\ge N\), the evaluator instantiates the finite prior and estimator records and computes the exact pair \((B_n,U_n)\in\mathbb A_{\mathrm R}^2\) satisfying \(B_n\le R_n(c)\le U_n\) and \(n^{4/3}(U_n-B_n)\le\eta\).

definitions.name: Normalization-preserving rational contrast brackets
definitions.construction: Within the fixed sign chamber of \(c\), choose \(c'\in\mathcal C_K\cap\mathbb Q^K\) with the same active support and signs, positive coefficients summing to \(1\), negative coefficients summing to \(-1\), and error measured by \(\omega(c,c')=\|c-c'\|_1/2\).

statements.statement: For every \(c\in\mathcal C_K\), the primal program defining \(V_c\) is feasible for every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{S_c}\), and \[V_c(\xi)=\max\{\ell^\top\xi:|\ell^\top b_t|\le\theta_t^2\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal T_c\}.\] The dual feasible set is compact on \(\mathbf 1^\perp\), \(V_c\) is finite, convex, even, continuous, and positively homogeneous, and \(0<\kappa(c)\le1\). For rational \(c\), primal and dual optimizers and \(\kappa(c)\) are exactly rational and terminate under finite linear programming.
statements.justification: The gauge is the finite-alphabet object that converts multi-arm response geometry into a scalar Airy coefficient.
statements.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1, has no response-alphabet linear program because its reduced experiment is scalar.
statements.consumer: The exact primal-dual record supplies both the shrinkage score and the rational input to the finite certificate.

statements.statement: For \(c=(1/3,2/3,-1/4,-3/4)\), exact primal and dual response-alphabet witnesses over all sixteen \(t\in\mathcal T_c\) give \(\kappa(c)=11/36\). The basis \(B=[v,d_1,d_2,d_3]\), with \(d_j\in\ker(c^\top)\), represents every missing-active-arm target direction, and adding an inactive fifth arm changes the allocation identity to \[H(q)-4=4\sum_{a\in S_c}(q_a-q_a^\star)^2/q_a+4\left(1-\sum_{a\in S_c}q_a\right).\]
statements.justification: This exact mixed-sign case is the earliest falsification test for the universal coefficient and every allocation-face identity.
statements.gap: The finite checks in the presolve draft are not an asymptotic or design-uniform theorem and have not appeared in the cited literature.
statements.consumer: A failed identity here terminates the universal program before costly weak-integration and certificate work.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(K\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C_K\), the independent allocation in \(\mathrm{def:independent\text{-}qstar\text{-}design}\) and the total estimator \(\delta_n^\star\) satisfy \[\sup_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}\mathcal R_n(\mathcal D_n^\star,\delta_n^\star;y)\le n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Equivalently, \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)\ge\Lambda_c\).
statements.justification: This constructs the contrast-specific nonlinear procedure that realizes the proposed coefficient.
statements.gap: The fixed-allocation multi-arm expansion does not establish that no dependent design has a larger second-order improvement.
statements.consumer: A prospective four-regimen trial obtains an explicit contrast-weighted allocation and full-label shrinkage rule.

statements.statement: Can the response-tube handle be completed into priors \(\Pi_n\), independent of the chosen assignment law, such that uniformly over every allocation-count vector \(r\), including every zero-count face, \[\operatorname{BR}_{\Pi_n}(r)\ge n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}-o(n^{-4/3}),\] with a remainder uniform over local counts, positive exterior counts, inactive-arm allocations, and missing-active-arm faces? The proof must establish exact posterior regression for the random finite-population target, weak integration by parts across all response-tube sign cells, and remainder bounds that remain valid after averaging over any dependent outcome-independent design and any randomized labeled-data estimator.
statements.justification: This is the genuine open proof boundary: it is the only step that excludes every dependent design at the sharp coefficient.
statements.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B, use a scalar ancillary transform; Hull (2026), Theorem 1, reduces a two-arm finite game but supplies no multi-arm all-face Airy prior.
statements.consumer: The inequality certifies that contrast-weighted independent assignment is second-order optimal among all outcome-independent randomizations.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(K\), every \(c\in\mathcal C_K\), every outcome-independent possibly dependent design \(\mathcal D_n\), and every possibly randomized full-label estimator \(\widehat\tau\), \[\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}\mathcal R_n(\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau;y)\ge n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\] where the remainder is uniform over the design-estimator pair. Equivalently, \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)\le\Lambda_c\).
statements.justification: The lower theorem turns a fixed-design Airy expansion into an unrestricted joint design-estimation result.
statements.gap: Bai (2023), Theorem 2.1, supplies permutation symmetrization; Theorem 3.1 reduces the minimax problem over linear-estimator schemes to minimization of a quadratic expected form subject to linear constraints over assignment and estimator schemes; and Theorem 3.2 gives the two-arm complete-randomization, Neyman-allocation, and difference-in-means specialization. These results do not control arbitrary binary schedules, nonlinear estimators, or the second-order coefficient.
statements.consumer: The theorem rules out correlated or face-supported randomizations that could otherwise invalidate the proposed clinical allocation.

statements.statement: Theorem 1. On the explicit union \[\{(2,(1,-1)),(2,(-1,1))\}\cup\{(K,c):K\ge3,\ c\in\mathcal C_K\},\] the unrestricted risk satisfies \[R_n(c)=n^{-1}-C_AV_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\qquad \lim_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)=\Lambda_c.\] On the at-least-three-active-arm component, the independent allocation \(q^\star\) and the total full-label nonlinear Airy estimator attain the expansion. On the published two-arm component, the two-arm reduction proposition gives \(V_c(s_c/2)=1\) and recovers Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1. Thus the union contains the published two-arm class as its first component and adds every fixed normalized contrast with at least three active arms as its second component, with the two-arm reduction providing the bridge.
statements.justification: The equality identifies both the universal Airy law and the contrast-specific response-alphabet curvature in the unrestricted multi-arm game.
statements.gap: The closest sharp theorem is the two-arm expansion of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026); no searched source gives a multi-arm response-alphabet coefficient or an all-face lower bound.
statements.consumer: For an ACTG-175-style four-regimen binary trial, the theorem determines whether the prespecified regimen-versus-average allocation and nonlinear shrinkage rule are second-order minimax.

statements.statement: For every rational \(c\in\mathcal C_K\cap\mathbb Q^K\) and every rational \(\eta>0\), \(\mathsf{Cert}(c,\eta)\) terminates with a finite symbolic record \(\Gamma\). The record contains \(N\), finite rational and real-algebraic data, proof-checkable monotone bounds, and an explicitly specified total evaluator \(\mathsf{Eval}_{\Gamma}\). For every requested integer \(n\ge N\), \[\mathsf{Eval}_{\Gamma}(n)=(B_n,U_n)\in\mathbb A_{\mathrm R}^2,\qquad B_n\le R_n(c)\le U_n,\qquad n^{4/3}(U_n-B_n)\le\eta.\] Each \(B_n\) is the exact Bayes risk of a finite-schedule prior valid against all outcome-independent designs, and each \(U_n\) is the exact worst-schedule risk of a rationalized total full-label rule under the independent allocation \(q^\star\). Real-algebraic values are represented by square-free integer polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and Thom-sign data, and every arithmetic or order operation is certified by exact rational algorithms. As a continuity corollary, every real \(c\in\mathcal C_K\) admits normalization-preserving rational brackets \(c'\) with the same active support and signs such that \[|\sqrt{R_n(c)}-\sqrt{R_n(c')}|\le\omega(c,c').\] Choosing bracket errors \(o(n^{-5/6})\) transfers the coefficient and risk expansion mathematically to \(c\), without asserting a Turing evaluator for an unrepresented real contrast.
statements.justification: An all-future exact certificate distinguishes a theorem-backed second-order recommendation from numerical convergence at selected sample sizes.
statements.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) and Hull (2026) give finite reductions, while Aronow and Lopatto (2026), Theorem 3, gives exact witnesses only under unbiasedness; none supplies this uniform multi-arm asymptotic certificate.
statements.consumer: Trial planners can certify at a given horizon whether the proposed independent allocation is within a chosen normalized risk tolerance of the unrestricted optimum, while rational enclosures support mathematical verification of prespecified real-valued weights.

statements.statement: For either normalized two-arm contrast \(c\in\{(1,-1),(-1,1)\}\), one has \(S_c=\{1,2\}\), \(q^\star=(1/2,1/2)\), and \(V_c(s_c/2)=1\). The universal formula therefore reduces to \(R_n(c)=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), exactly the expansion in Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1. This equality is the bridge from the published two-arm component to the new at-least-three-active-arm component of Theorem 1.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check on the coefficient normalization and Airy scaling.
statements.gap: This proposition reproduces the published scalar special case and is not claimed as a novel theorem contribution.
statements.consumer: It lets readers audit the multi-arm notation and coefficient against the known two-arm benchmark.

sampling_model.design: Before outcomes are observed, the designer chooses any outcome-independent probability law on \(\mathcal A_K^n\), including laws with dependent assignments. The explicit attaining design assigns independently with \(q_a^\star=|c_a|/2\) on the active arms.
sampling_model.units: The population consists of \(n\) fixed labeled units. Each unit has a fixed binary potential outcome under every arm, and the only randomness in risk is assignment and optional estimator randomization.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one label in \(\mathcal A_K\) is assigned to each unit; the estimator observes the full assignment vector and the realized binary outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: The unrestricted game imposes no overlap restriction. The proposed lower bound explicitly covers every allocation-count face, including a zero count for one or more active arms and assignments to inactive arms.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The nonlinear upper rule uses the finite response-alphabet dual score, and the lower bound uses a finite-schedule prior localized along the target direction and all contrast-orthogonal directions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted binary two-arm minimax risk is \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), attained by Bernoulli randomization and nonlinear shrinkage.
For bounded two-arm potential outcomes, independent assignment remains minimax when measurable estimators are unrestricted.

Theorem 2.1 gives permutation symmetrization and complete-randomization content, Theorem 3.1 reduces the minimax problem over linear-estimator schemes to minimization of a quadratic expected form subject to linear constraints over assignment and estimator schemes, and Theorem 3.2 gives the two-arm complete-randomization, Neyman-allocation, and difference-in-means specialization.

For two-arm controlled experiments, complete randomization is minimax for effect-estimation precision under a permutation-symmetric conditional-mean class, and inference-constrained mixed strategies optimize precision subject to design-uniformity constraints.
Under unbiased estimation of bounded finite-population totals, pairwise-independent sampling attains a sharp minimax bound.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.
Design-based estimators and variance adjustments are developed for pairwise contrasts in multi-armed randomized trials.
Adaptive treatment assignments are optimized for final multi-arm Stein-like shrinkage estimators by evaluating heteroscedastic Gaussian shrinkage risk.

tldr: On the explicit union of the published normalized two-arm class and the new class of fixed normalized binary contrasts with at least three active arms, the unrestricted finite-population design-estimation game has a universal Airy correction whose contrast dependence is exactly the finite response-alphabet gauge \(V_c(s_c/2)\). Contrast-weighted independent assignment and a total full-label nonlinear estimator attain the coefficient on the new component, while the two-arm reduction bridges to the published component. A full-dimensional piecewise-polynomial finite-schedule prior must establish the matching lower bound uniformly over dependent designs and every zero-count face. For rational contrasts, a terminating algorithm returns a finite proof-checkable certificate record and a total evaluator that generates exact risk brackets at each requested future sample size; rational bracketing transfers the mathematical expansion, but not Turing evaluation, to arbitrary real contrasts.

project_justification.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 2.2 and 3.1, solve the unrestricted binary two-arm game through a scalar ancillary experiment and an Airy least-favorable prior. Hull (2026), Theorem 1, independently reduces the bounded two-arm game. Neither construction handles a signed contrast with a multidimensional nuisance kernel, a response alphabet of size \(2^{|S_c|}\), or allocation faces that omit an active arm.
project_justification.niche: The response-alphabet gauge isolates the contrast-specific cusp while a basis consisting of the target direction and \(\ker(c^\top)\) supplies target-changing directions invisible on every missing-arm face. This geometry can support a single prior whose conditional Bayes risk is uniform over every realized count vector and hence every dependent outcome-independent design.
project_justification.fill: The paper will prove the Airy headline on the explicit union of the published normalized two-arm class and the new at-least-three-active-arm class, with the two-arm reduction as the bridge; identify \(C_AV_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}\); construct the explicit independent design and nonlinear estimator on the new component; and provide a finite proof-checkable certificate record with a total exact per-sample-size evaluator for rational inputs. The central open content is the exact-target weak integration-by-parts inequality and its uniform local, exterior, inactive-arm, and zero-count remainder control.

related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 2.1--2.3 and 3.1 and Appendix C, provide the writing and estimation exemplars: a finite scalar reduction, nonlinear Airy shrinkage, and discretized least-favorable priors for two arms. Hull (2026), Theorem 1 and its three-step symmetrization proof, shows that bounded outcomes can favor independent assignment even with arbitrary measurable estimators, but remains two-arm. Bai (2023), Theorem 2.1, establishes permutation symmetrization and the associated complete-randomization content; Theorem 3.1 reduces the minimax problem over linear-estimator schemes to minimization of a quadratic expected form subject to linear constraints over assignment and estimator schemes; and Theorem 3.2 gives the two-arm complete-randomization, Neyman-allocation, and difference-in-means specialization. Those restrictions do not settle the present fixed-schedule nonlinear game. Kallus (2021) studies minimax precision in two-arm controlled experiments over a conditional-mean class with a minimax-variance objective, proving complete randomization under permutation symmetry and constructing inference-constrained mixed-strategy designs; its objective and admissible design class differ from worst-schedule squared risk over binary potential outcomes with arbitrary outcome-independent assignments and unrestricted labeled-data estimators. Aronow and Lopatto (2026), Theorems 2 and 3, retain exact finite arithmetic for bounded totals but impose unbiasedness. Levit (1986) supplies the positive-eigenfunction architecture linking second-order minimax risk and a Schrodinger ground state. Rosenman and Hunter (2026) optimize sequential adaptive assignments for final multi-arm Stein-like shrinkage estimators by evaluating heteroscedastic Gaussian shrinkage risk; that adaptive Gaussian decision problem is distinct from minimax risk over fixed binary schedules, arbitrary outcome-independent assignment laws, and unrestricted labeled-data estimators. Schochet (2018) supplies conventional design-based multi-arm estimators but does not motivate the proposal-specific requirement of at least three active contrast coordinates. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies the four-regimen application rather than a theorem comparator.
honest_scope: The new multi-arm theorem is pointwise in every fixed permitted contrast and fixed arm count; the headline is stated on the explicit union with the published normalized two-arm class, connected by the two-arm reduction. It makes no growing-arm or vanishing-weight-uniform claim. The effective theorem accepts rational contrasts and rational tolerances and returns a finite symbolic record containing a total exact evaluator for requested integers beyond its threshold. Its continuity corollary transfers the mathematical coefficient to real contrasts but does not claim computation from an unrepresented real. Weak-null inference, covariate balancing, and interval-valued endpoint reduction are separate follow-on questions. The all-count exact-target Bayes inequality is explicitly open and is not disguised as an assumption.

Rebuttal: unequal signed weights and zero-count faces retain contrast-orthogonal information and cannot be represented by a scalar collapse; the design-uniform Bayes bridge is new.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Generalize the conditional Bernoulli rounding and Jensen reduction while preserving a signed multi-arm target and unrestricted design quantifiers.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found exact bounded two-arm reductions and standard multi-arm contrast inference, but no published multi-arm endpoint theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: coordinatewise Bernoulli rounding makes the result immediate. Rebuttal: the exact zero-sum target identity does extend, so this becomes a corollary once the binary universal theorem is proved and is not a standalone kernel.

seed_details.kernel: For a fixed finite nonbinary outcome alphabet, derive whether the second-order constant is an endpoint gauge or a genuinely alphabet-dependent polyhedral potential.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace binary affine regression of the target on each observed marginal by the finite-category conditional projection and identify the limiting cusp.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite response alphabet, multi-arm contrast, and Airy minimax design found no occupied target-method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Theorem 2.3 of the anchor already reduces every bounded alphabet to endpoints. Rebuttal: its result is two-arm; however the same rounding argument is likely to subsume the fixed finite alphabet after the binary multi-arm theorem, so this is not competitive.

literature_map: The selected kernel adapts Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 2.1--2.3 and 3.1 and Appendices B--C: its scalar ancillary transform and one-dimensional Airy prior are the precise proof steps that fail with three or more active arms. Hull (2026), Theorem 1 and Appendix A.4, confirms unrestricted-estimator finite-game symmetrization for bounded two-arm outcomes but supplies no multi-arm coefficient. Bai (2023), Theorem 2.1, provides permutation symmetrization and complete-randomization content; Theorem 3.1 reduces the minimax problem over linear-estimator schemes to minimization of a quadratic expected form subject to linear constraints over assignment and estimator schemes; and Theorem 3.2 gives the two-arm complete-randomization, Neyman-allocation, and difference-in-means specialization. Its permutation-invariant distribution classes and linear schemes do not cover arbitrary fixed binary schedules and nonlinear second-order risk. Kallus (2021) studies two-arm minimax design for effect-estimation precision over a conditional-mean class, using a minimax-variance objective and inference-constrained mixed strategies; this is distinct from worst-schedule squared risk over binary fixed schedules, arbitrary outcome-independent design laws, and unrestricted estimators. Aronow and Lopatto (2026), Theorems 2 and 3, demonstrate exact witness-level minimaxity under unbiasedness but do not connect finite arithmetic to an unrestricted Airy tail. Levit (1986) provides the ground-state proof architecture. Rosenman and Hunter (2026) study adaptive multi-arm allocation under heteroscedastic Gaussian risk for Stein-like shrinkage estimators, rather than the present fixed-schedule unrestricted minimax game. Schochet (2018) supplies conventional design-based multi-arm estimators but does not supply the proposal-specific active-support restriction, and Hammer et al. (1996) supplies a four-regimen consumer. Exact searches on the multi-arm target-method pair and on papers citing the August 2026 anchor found no closer theorem that subsumes the response-alphabet coefficient, the all-allocation-face lower bound, or the finite all-future certificate.
novelty_justification: The closest sharp result treats the normalized two-arm class through a scalar ancillary experiment. The headline is stated on the explicit union of that published class and the new class of every fixed signed contrast with at least three active coordinates, with an exact two-arm reduction as the bridge. On the new component, the coefficient is derived from all response types through a polyhedral gauge, and one finite-schedule prior must be valid uniformly across positive, exterior, inactive, and zero-active-count faces against arbitrary dependent designs. No located paper gives this coefficient, converse, or finite proof-checkable all-future certificate.
message: The revised core preserves the universal multi-arm Airy law, accurately characterizes Bai (2023), adds Kallus (2021), and folds real-contrast continuity into the finite-certificate corollary.
